Tabulate the edges and nodes of an htna network

Source: R/methods-htna.R
as.data.frame.htna.Rd

as.data.frame() returns the edges or the nodes of a heterogeneous transition network as a tidy data frame in which every row carries the actor type of its codes. The edge table lists every non-zero transition with its weight and the actor types of its source and target, so the within-actor and between-actor transitions (for example Human to AI) can be read, counted or filtered directly. The node table lists every code with its actor type.

For a grouped network the tables of all cohorts are stacked with a leading group column. Self-transitions (the diagonal of the weight matrix) are kept. For an undirected network (method = "co_occurrence") each pair of codes is listed once.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'htna'
as.data.frame(
  x,
  row.names = NULL,
  optional = FALSE,
  ...,
  what = c("edges", "nodes")
)

# S3 method for class 'htna_group'
as.data.frame(
  x,
  row.names = NULL,
  optional = FALSE,
  ...,
  what = c("edges", "nodes")
)

Arguments

x

An htna network from build_htna() or an htna_group.

row.names, optional

Ignored; present for the generic.

...

Unused.

what

"edges" (default) or "nodes".

Value

A data frame. For what = "edges": one row per non-zero edge, with columns from, to, weight, source_actor and target_actor (factors in the network's actor order), sorted by source then target in node order. For what = "nodes": one row per node, with columns node and actor. Grouped networks add a first column group.

See also

build_htna(), summary.htna() for counts per actor pair.

Examples

data(human_ai)
net <- build_htna(human_ai, actor_type = "actor_type")
#> Metadata aggregated per session: ties resolved by first occurrence in 'session_date' (1 sessions), 'cluster' (42 sessions), 'actor_type' (24 sessions)
head(as.data.frame(net))
#>   from        to     weight source_actor target_actor
#> 1  Ask       Ask 0.01823579           AI           AI
#> 2  Ask     Check 0.06318914           AI        Human
#> 3  Ask   Execute 0.02205259           AI           AI
#> 4  Ask Frustrate 0.11577608           AI        Human
#> 5  Ask   Inquire 0.06318914           AI        Human
#> 6  Ask      Plan 0.40882103           AI           AI
as.data.frame(net, what = "nodes")
#>         node actor
#> 1        Ask    AI
#> 2      Check Human
#> 3   Delegate    AI
#> 4    Execute    AI
#> 5  Frustrate Human
#> 6    Inquire Human
#> 7       Plan    AI
#> 8     Refine Human
#> 9     Repair    AI
#> 10    Report    AI
#> 11   Request Human
#> 12   Specify Human
